title: Joining the Camellia band and the repertoire
summary: He joined John Smith's Camellia band with George Thompson (Stuart) and Morris Asano, playing old Dixieland numbers.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I joined the Camellia band, that's right.
Well how was that band set up? Who was the leader and the manager?
A fellow by the name of John Smith.
Yeah, I had George Thompson, which everybody knew him by the name of George Stuart.
Oh yeah. You heard Bonk talk about that.
He was a fine clarinet man.
But his real name was what, Thompson?
Thompson. They told me his mother was named Stuart, so everybody called him George Stuart. But of course it might have been a case like me with this Fernandez.
And did you have a trombone player in the band?

Yeah I had a trombone player, a fellow Morris Asano. He's still living, he don't play, he don't care about playing. How old is he? Well Morris should be about 50, in his 50s, in his early 50s I imagine. About 54, 55 like that.
And what kind of music did these bands play? Howard and Henry Allen and the Camelia that was there.

Well they played the numbers that they're playing the dead, the Dixieland numbers like Piano Moore and Dogtown Struthers Ball and Clarinet Marmalet and Fidgeted Feet. The fact that they played all the old numbers that they're using the dead that's in demand.
